tasks.name: T212 demo: hourly trader + monitor
tasks.command_summary: bash trading/monitor_run.sh; python3 -m t212bot decide ... --execute; commit and push
tasks.prompt:
Hourly trading-decision and monitor run for the Trading 212 PRACTICE (demo) account (branch claude/trading212-agent-skills-r71zy3). The owner chose (2026-10-14) to have Claude trade the whole demo account intraday to make as much money as possible, 3x ETPs allowed. strategy.json is in mode "discretionary".

1. Run: bash trading/monitor_run.sh  (sync + read-only checks; exit 0 ok, 1 warn, 2 critical). Read its output and alerts.
2. If the LSE is open for trading (08:15-16:15 London, weekdays) and nothing CRITICAL is unresolved, make a decision:
   - Gather real data only: intraday bars (Yahoo chart API, interval 5m/15m/60m) for QQQ, NQ=F, ES=F, GC=F, LQQ3.L, EQQQ.L, VUAG.L, SGLN.L, 3LGO.L; the 100-day trend state from the monitor; and a quick WebSearch for market-moving news today (Fed/CPI/earnings/geopolitics). Never invent numbers.
   - Choose target weights over the universe in strategy.json decision_limits (LQQ3l_EQ, EQQQl_EQ, VUAGl_EQ, SGLNl_EQ, 3LGO1l_EQ), long-only, sum <= 1, or all cash. "No change" is a valid and often best decision: each switch costs roughly 0.1-0.3% in spread, so only trade when the expected move clearly exceeds that.
   - If changing: cd trading && python3 -m t212bot decide --set TICKER=W ... --reason "<data-based reason, 1-2 sentences>" --execute   (or --cash). Then commit trading/config/discretionary_targets.json and trading/journal and push (rebase and retry on conflict).
3. At the 20:57 run (after the US close): write a short scorecard in trading/journal/scorecard.md (append): today's account return vs B_live_rules_at_close (trend rule shadow) and A_benchmark_vwrp from `python3 -m t212bot report` / PERFORMANCE.md, decisions made, cumulative since 2026-10-14. Commit and push. Tell the owner plainly if discretionary trading is behind the trend rule.
4. Notify the owner (one line) for each executed trade, any WARN/CRITICAL that needs attention, and the evening scorecard. Otherwise reply in one line and do not notify.
5. Fix genuine bugs in trading/ with a regression test (cd trading && python3 -m pytest -q must pass).

Hard rules: orders only via `python3 -m t212bot decide` or the ops run; never weaken a safety check or the decision limits (max 8 decisions/day, -10% daily stop to cash); demo only - never contact live.trading212.com; respect trading/KILL; never print or commit credentials.

tasks.name: T212 demo: trading ops
tasks.command_summary: git sync; bash trading/ops_run.sh (python3 -m t212bot run --execute)
tasks.prompt:
Scheduled trading-ops run for the Trading 212 PRACTICE (demo) account bot (branch claude/trading212-agent-skills-r71zy3, already checked out in this session). The account owner authorised this bot to trade the demo account autonomously.

1. Sync: git fetch origin claude/trading212-agent-skills-r71zy3 && git checkout claude/trading212-agent-skills-r71zy3 && git pull --rebase origin claude/trading212-agent-skills-r71zy3
2. Check (without printing values) that T212_ENV equals "demo" and T212_API_KEY / T212_API_SECRET are set. If not, stop and report which is missing.
3. Run exactly: bash trading/ops_run.sh   (tests, then `python3 -m t212bot run --execute` which trades only if a rebalance is due and the LSE is open, then regenerates trading/PERFORMANCE.md, commits the journal and pushes).
4. Report briefly from its output, the newest trading/journal/events.jsonl entries and trading/PERFORMANCE.md: run status, orders/fills/slippage if any, account value vs shadow benchmarks, errors.
5. On failure (non-zero exit, failed tests, run_failed, order_ambiguous, order_rejected): find the root cause; fix genuine bugs in trading/ with a regression test (cd trading && python3 -m pytest -q must pass), commit and push. Never weaken a safety check.

Hard rules: demo only - never contact live.trading212.com; never place/modify/cancel orders except via `python3 -m t212bot`; never print or commit credentials; respect trading/KILL. If nothing noteworthy happened, keep the report to two lines, and send a push notification only for trades, failures or anything needing the owner's attention.

tasks.name: T212 demo: research loop
tasks.command_summary: git sync; follow research/LOOP.md (may change trading/config/strategy.json via PROMOTION_GATE)
tasks.prompt:
Research-loop run for the self-improving quantitative research system of the £100 Trading 212 PRACTICE (demo) account (branch claude/trading212-agent-skills-r71zy3, checked out in this session). The account owner asked for continuous research that keeps finding and testing better approaches until they say stop.

First: git fetch origin claude/trading212-agent-skills-r71zy3 && git checkout claude/trading212-agent-skills-r71zy3 && git pull --rebase origin claude/trading212-agent-skills-r71zy3

Then follow research/LOOP.md exactly: pick the next item from research/AGENDA.md, research it rigorously (pre-registered grids, costs, out-of-sample tests, bootstrap vs the champion, deflated Sharpe with the cumulative trial count), and apply research/PROMOTION_GATE.md before anything may change trading/config/strategy.json. Reuse code in research/ and trading/. Context: an earlier test run (2026-10-13) reached these conclusions but could not push them, so re-run them properly here: P1 volatility-managed momentum - rejected (DSR 0.86-0.90 < 0.90, no edge on the real ETFs); P2 trend-filtered momentum sleeve - rejected (lower OOS CAGR than champion; insurance only).

Hard rules: demo only - never contact live.trading212.com; never place, modify or cancel orders (the ops run trades); never invent data or results - every number must come from code you ran and committed; never print or commit credentials; if research/STOP exists, log that and end. Prefer 'no change' when in doubt. Commit and push (rebase and retry on conflict). Finish with a 5-line summary: item, what ran, key numbers, decision, next item. Push-notify the owner only if a challenger enters shadow or is promoted, or if something is broken.
